evidence.asserts: no relation this page reads hides a refusal inside an empty successful response
evidence.checked: PASSES. Of this page's 7 read relation(s), 2 were probed live at the gateway (resume_documents, resume_versions). None of them returns an identical status and body type to an anon caller and a member, so a refusal here is observably different from absence. THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

findings.title: selector pointed at the container, not this subject
findings.detail: WITHDRAWN BY ME, same turn, before anyone relied on it. I banked this from page_component_selectors.json, and an audit of that map against the bank's own subject NAMES found this entry points at the wrong element: the subject is a ROW/CARD and my selector was its CONTAINER (or a generic utility class like .btn/.ic/.card that matches unrelated furniture). Measuring a container and recording it against a row subject is exactly the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this scoped prover was built to END - I reintroduced it one level up, in the map rather than the reading. The reading itself was real; it was just a reading of something else. Returned to owed pending a corrected selector.

findings.detail: Measured with the locally-built 1.4.3 instrument described on the passing rows of this same oracle, self-tested 24/24 in both directions, over a denominator with 0 abstentions - so these are not artefacts of an unresolved background. one shared muted-text token: 28 nodes at exactly 3.92:1 against rgb(29,43,62), 10.5-10.9px, spanning div.sec-sub, p and label. NOT BANKED, and the row stays owed: the fix comes first and the row is earned after, which is the fix-before-bank rule. Two cautions for whoever takes it: first, these are SMALL text at 9.3-12px, exactly the band where WCAG 2.x and APCA disagree most - the APCA row for this page passes, and both oracles are supposed to hold, so the fix must not be to relax either one. Second, the same sweep produced one FABRICATED severe failure before the instrument was corrected (dayplanner's clip-text logo read as white-on-orange at 1.72:1), so each of these should be confirmed against its own computed style before any token is changed. resume's 28 all sit at exactly 3.92:1 against rgb(29,43,62), which is the signature of ONE shared muted-text token rather than 28 separate decisions - a single central fix, in the shape of the platform-wide ::placeholder and wayfinding-chip fixes already made in this arc.

findings.title: DENOMINATOR CORRECTED 32 -> 36 tab stops; verdict unchanged at 0 without an indicator
findings.detail: THE PREVIOUS SWEEP UNDER-COUNTED THIS DENOMINATOR, and the cause was a break where a continue belonged. Focus order on these pages runs shared chrome, then BODY, then the page own controls - so a loop that treated a BODY-focus stop as the end of the tab ring stopped walking before reaching any page control. On assistant that reported ZERO stops against 9 real ones and I held the row back as either vacuous or a WCAG 2.1.1 failure; it was neither, it was my loop. Re-run with BODY as a CONTINUE, a 120-press budget and a 25-press no-new-stop stall guard. On this page the truncation cost 4 stops (32 counted, 36 real). The VERDICT is unchanged - 0 of 36 lacked a visible indicator on the full walk - so the row is not withdrawn. But the banked denominator was narrower than the page, and a narrowed denominator is the exact flaw this bank exists to catch: 0 failing over a subset is a weaker claim than 0 failing over the whole. Recorded rather than silently re-stamped, because the difference between those two claims is the whole point.
findings.observed: 32 stops counted vs 36 on the corrected walk; 0 without indicator either way

findings.detail: RECORDED OWED FOR HAVING NO SUBJECT, NOT PASSED: #resume-manager renders **0 icon-only controls** among its 3 interactive controls - every one carries visible text. A zero here is indistinguishable from a dialog that labelled everything correctly, so crediting it would be the same false green as a comparison over an empty set. TO FINISH: this account has no saved resumes, and the per-resume rows (rename/duplicate/delete affordances) are where icon-only controls would live - seed a saved resume, then re-walk. MEASURED INSIDE #resume-manager ONLY, so V3's numbers are V3's, at 390 CSS px (layout read back). REACHED BY THE PAGE'S OWN CONTROL - the '📂 My Resumes' button - found by matching its text WITHOUT anchors, because the label leads with an emoji and an anchored /^my resumes/ misses it (that exact mistake cost a probe on the sibling preview dialog). resume.html carries NO onclick attributes at all; every trigger is wired with addEventListener, so text matching is the route. The settle was a waitForFunction on the dialog becoming visible with real height, not a fixed sleep. AND THE SUBJECT WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE ROADMAP BEFORE BANKING: resume's banked subjects are V1 builder, V2 review sheet, V3 resume manager, with preview-overlay in the deferred TAIL. The preview dialog also measures clean but is deliberately NOT banked here - attaching real evidence to the wrong row is the same error class as measuring an unarrived page, and harder to catch because the numbers look healthy. DENOMINATOR STATED HONESTLY: 3 interactive controls and 8 rendered leaves. The dialog is genuinely populated - it renders its purpose copy ('Keep separate resumes for different jobs, e.g. a maintenance CV and an OFW...') - but this account has NO SAVED RESUMES, so the manager's LIST is empty. These three oracles are about the dialog's own chrome and hold over what is rendered; anything about list ROWS (component states, populated counts) is not settled by this reading and stays owed.

evidence.asserts: after saving, the surface names what changed and where it now lives
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK. The confirmation reads: '✓ Resume saved → backed up to your account now, and on this device. The previous version is kept in your history.' I WROTE THE CLAUSES AFTER THE ARROW THIS WALK. The shipped copy was '✓ Resume saved.', which states that something happened but not what a person can rely on afterwards - and on THIS page that matters more than most, because the entire promise of the page is that their work survives. The sentence claims exactly what the path does and nothing more: it upserts resume_documents (the cloud copy tied to their account), writes the on-device copy through saveLocal(), and has already taken a snapshotVersion('before save') into resume_versions, pruned to the ten most recent. THE OTHER TWO BRANCHES WERE ALREADY EXEMPLARY AND ARE UNCHANGED, which is worth recording because it is the standard the success branch had fallen below: signed out it says 'Saved on this device. Sign in to back up to the cloud.' and offline it says 'Offline: saved on this device, will sync later.' Both name exactly where the work is and what is still owed. REACHED ON THE BUILDER ITSELF. #btn-save is not reachable on a bare load - which is why an earlier enumeration of this page reported zero commit controls - so the walk waits for it, types into #rb-field-name so there is something to save, and stamps a data-* attribute on the control rather than an id. That last detail is deliberate: overwriting an id is how a probe silently breaks a page's own guard, which is exactly what happened on analytics, where the handler looked its own button up by id in order to disable it.

findings.title: FAILS: with 8 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 1798 characters before the refusal and 1798 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than I
findings.detail: FAILS: with 8 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 1798 characters before the refusal and 1798 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. The platform already has the pieces - a central WRITE-failure message and the correct 401-vs-403 discriminator in utils.js - but there is no equivalent on the READ path, so a refused read renders as dashes or blanks with no explanation. On logbook the numbers '516 entries 30 machines 6 open' became '- entries - machines - open' with the body text identical to the character (1107 before and after) and not one word about why. A person cannot tell 'there is no data' from 'the load failed' from 'you are not allowed', and those three call for three different actions. THE FIX IS ONE ADOPTION, not 15 edits: give the read path the same treatment the write path already has. This independently reproduces a finding already recorded as 'the message already exists; the gap is ADOPTION on the read path'. SCOPE: V1, the page as it loads, and READ refusal only - a refused WRITE is a different path with its own central message, and is not claimed here. 5 of the 22 pages are excluded from the sweep because they are public or have no authenticated read to refuse. The walk is NON-WRITING.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_number_labelled.mjs, RE-RUN THIS SESSION - 79 number-bearing elements across the roster, 79 labelled, 0 unlabelled.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_number_labelled.mjs, RE-RUN THIS SESSION - 79 number-bearing elements across the roster, 79 labelled, 0 unlabelled. ★THE DEFINITION IS DELIBERATELY NARROW, because a loose one makes this worthless. A number-bearing element is a LEAF whose trimmed text is numeric-only after stripping currency, separators, % and a unit suffix: '9', '₱1,850,000' and '61%' qualify; '9 open items carried over' does NOT, because it labels itself. And a LABEL is non-numeric text of >=3 characters in the element's own aria-label or title, or in an ANCESTOR's text once the number itself is removed - which is how this platform actually builds stat tiles, with the figure in one span and its name in a sibling. ★THE PROVER CARRIES ITS OWN POSITIVE CONTROL, and every page reports ctl=ok: an element that SHOULD be caught is injected and must be caught. Without that, '0 unlabelled' is indistinguishable from a detector that finds nothing at all - the empty-denominator failure this bank keeps catching. ★AND THE EVIDENCE IS FRESH ON PURPOSE. A clean report from yesterday already existed and I did NOT bank from it: I edited eleven pages this session, so any claim resting on them was staled by my own changes. Re-running a read-only prover is cheaper than reasoning about whether an edit mattered - the same call made for the double-fire run. FOR THIS PAGE: it rendered NO number-bearing element in this state, so there is nothing for the oracle to judge. Recorded as measured-and-empty rather than passed - '0 unlabelled of 0' is the vacuous green this bank refuses.

findings.title: LEFT OWED with a full diagnosis rather than graded, because this view carries the page's highest-stakes promise and a plausible-looking pass here would be worse than an honest gap.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED with a full diagnosis rather than graded, because this view carries the page's highest-stakes promise and a plausible-looking pass here would be worse than an honest gap. WHAT V2 IS, established this walk: #review-sheet, titled 'Review what we found' with the instruction 'Uncheck anything you don't want. Tap a value to edit', a #review-body checklist, and two controls - #review-cancel and #review-confirm, whose label counts the selection ('Add selected (n)'). It is driven by openReview(title, items, onConfirm), where each item is {group, label, value, checked} and renders BOTH a checkbox (data-review-check=i) and an EDITABLE value input (data-review-value=i). That is the mechanism behind the promise the page makes in two languages: nothing enters the resume without confirmation. WHY IT IS NOT GRADED YET, precisely. openReview is PAGE-SCOPED, not a global, so it cannot be called from a probe - the same trap that defeated a wrapper attempt on skillmatrix's openExam in this same session. The only honest route in is the real one: put a file through the upload, let the client parse it, and let the resume-extract edge function answer. That call is made with a raw fetchWithTimeout (not functions.invoke), so a window.fetch shim does reach it, and its contract is known: the page reads {ok, data} or a bare object, treats raw.ok === false or raw.error as failure, and has a distinct PARTIAL branch ('Read X of Y sections - one page was busy. Re-upload to add the rest.'). What is NOT yet established is the field shape INSIDE data that the mapper turns into review items - that is the one missing piece, and it must be read from the mapper rather than guessed, or the walk would be grading a payload I invented against a gate that never saw real extraction. WHAT THE NEXT WALK SHOULD DO: read the extract-to-items mapper for its field names, synthesize a faithful {ok:true, data:{...}} response, upload a small text file through the real input, and then measure the four things this gate exists for - that NOTHING is applied before #review-confirm is pressed, that unchecking an item excludes it, that editing a value carries the EDIT rather than the original, and that the count in 'Add selected (n)' tracks the selection. The PARTIAL branch deserves its own reading, because 'read 6 of 9 sections' is the difference between a resume with a known gap and one the owner thinks is complete.

evidence.asserts: the review sheet says what will happen to the extracted items and what the person can do before it happens
evidence.checked: MEASURED LIVE via the real upload path (resume-extract intercepted, no model call, no writes). The sheet states the next step BEFORE the commit rather than after it, which is the right place for this view: its subtitle reads 'Uncheck anything you don't want. Tap a value to edit it before adding.' - naming both affordances and the fact that nothing is added yet - and the confirm button carries a LIVE count, 'Add selected (6)', which updates as items are checked and unchecked (measured 3 -> 2 when one was unchecked). So a person can see exactly how many items are about to enter their resume, and that they are the one who decides. That matters more here than on most views because this page's promise is explicitly that nothing enters the resume without confirmation, made in two places in the upload card; this sheet IS that promise's mechanism, and it holds. The items also carry provenance - each row renders a source chip (srcChip) and a 'Was: ...' label - so the person can see which upload a value came from, and rows that duplicate something already in the resume arrive UNCHECKED with '(already in your resume)' appended to the label. AND WHEN THE READ WAS INCOMPLETE, the sheet does not pretend otherwise: a partial extract opens the same sheet plus 'Read 2 of 3 sections - one page was busy. Re-upload to add the rest.', so 'what happens next' includes what did NOT happen. NOT CLAIMED: the post-confirm merge message. The confirm handler hands the selected items to a caller-supplied onConfirm (the sheet is shared by the upload path and runAutofill), so what the page says AFTER the merge belongs to those callers and was not walked here.

evidence.asserts: each resume-manager action says what it did and what it means afterwards
evidence.checked: MEASURED LIVE with the list fixtured and every DELETE held. THE DELETE CONFIRMATION WAS CORRECTED, because it named neither the scope nor the finality of what it had just done: it read 'Resume deleted.' while deleteResume removes the resume_documents row AND every resume_versions row for it. That history is the same history the save confirmation promises is being kept for the worker ('The previous version is kept in your history'), so a bare 'deleted' left them with no way to know it had gone too. It now reads 'Resume deleted - it and all of its saved versions are gone for good.', verified live in #toast-msg. THE OTHER TWO PATHS ALREADY NAMED THEIR EFFECT AND WERE LEFT ALONE: switching reads 'Opened "<title>".' and, before loading, saves the current resume if it is worth saving (resumeWorthSaving -> saveCloud) and clears the undo stack - whose own comment records why, that an Undo after switching would restore resume A's model while _resumeId points at B and the next save would write A's content into B's row; 'New blank resume' reads 'Started a new blank resume. Edit it, then tap 💾 Save.', which names the next action and where. A FAILED open is also legible: with ids that cannot resolve, the toast reads 'Could not open that resume.', the manager STAYS open and the list re-renders, so the person is left where they can try again rather than on a half-switched page. NOT CLAIMED: the successful 'Opened "<title>"' toast was not observed, because the fixture's synthetic ids cannot be loaded by loadCloudById - what was measured on that path is the failure, and it behaves correctly.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

observed.why: no composer reachable for this identity on this page
observed.not_green_because: a journey that cannot be constructed is unbuilt, not passing
observed.to_settle: add the missing composer to dialog_targets.mjs, or declared-na under R10 with the CO family as replacement

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_abandon_resume.mjs - the capture surface opened, filled with a marker only this run could produce, then ABANDONED BY RELOAD. An X is CANCELLING, which pages handle deliberately; a reload is what happens when a phone dies, and no confirm dialog can intercept it. ★THREE SHAPES, judged separately: a ROW THAT SHOULD NOT EXIST; a DRAFT THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS A DRAFT (a restored draft is the GOOD design - judged on the LABEL, never on the restoration); and a QUEUED WRITE draining later. The fill is proven to have landed, so no green is vacuous.  ★THIS PAGE IS THE REAL TEST OF THE DRAFT CLAUSE, because it autosaves LOCALLY on a 700ms debounce (scheduleLocalSave -> idbPut). Fields coming back after a reload would be the FEATURE, not a fault - so the question is whether the surface would SAY the restored text is a local draft rather than something saved to the account, on a page whose entire promise is that a person's work survives. Measured: nothing was written to resume_documents and nothing returned pre-filled, so the clause is satisfied on the clean-slate branch rather than the labelled-draft one. ★A QUERY DETAIL WORTH KEEPING: `doc` is JSONB, so LIKE needs an explicit ::text cast. Without it psql errors and the case reports ERROR rather than a verdict - the right failure, because a broken query's 0 rows is indistinguishable from a page that wrote nothing. RESULT: 0 row(s) created, 0 field(s) pre-filled - no row was written and nothing came back pre-filled - a clean slate

scenarios.oracle: a wrong entry can be corrected without starting over

evidence.asserts: this view refuses nothing on content, so there is no refusal-and-recovery to grade
evidence.checked: NOT APPLICABLE, and the reason is a design decision rather than an omission. MEASURED: the string 'required' appears ZERO times in resume.html, and saveCloud() validates no field - its only two guards are identity and connectivity, and NEITHER refuses the work: signed out it saves on the device and says 'Saved on this device. Sign in to back up to the cloud.', offline it saves on the device and says 'Offline: saved on this device, will sync later.' There is no content a person can enter that this page will decline to keep. THAT IS RIGHT FOR THIS PAGE. A resume is written in fragments over time; a builder that refused a half-finished entry would lose the fragment, and the fragment is the thing worth keeping. The 'correction' this oracle looks for is simply editing again - which is free here - and the page backs that with version history: every save takes a snapshotVersion('before save') into resume_versions, pruned to the ten most recent, so a wrong edit is recoverable rather than merely re-typeable. WHERE THE REAL REFUSAL-SHAPED GUARANTEE ON THIS PAGE LIVES, so this disposition is not read as 'the page checks nothing': it is the CONFIRM step on V2, where extracted content must be approved before it enters the resume - the page promises that in two languages - and the privacy claim that uploaded files are read only to fill the resume and then discarded. Those are that view's rows and this page's highest-stakes domain truth, and they are not satisfied by anything recorded here. evidence.checked: THIS IS THE VIEW'S ENTIRE PURPOSE AND IT WORKS, measured rather than inferred. findings.title: LEFT OWED WITH A SPLIT, MEASURED PICTURE.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED WITH A SPLIT, MEASURED PICTURE. WHAT IS PROTECTED: deletion is guarded by a genuine two-tap inline confirm - the first tap on ✕ writes nothing (measured 0/0), and the destructive step now also disables itself and states its finality ('Resume deleted - it and all of its saved versions are gone for good.'). Switching resumes is itself reversible - switch back - and switchResume saves the current resume before loading another, so a mis-tap does not cost unsaved work. WHAT CANNOT BE CORRECTED: a DELETED resume, absolutely. deleteResume removes the resume_documents row and every resume_versions row for it, there is no soft-delete column and no undo path, and the page's own _undoStack is in-memory and explicitly cleared on switch/new. So the confirm gate is the only protection that exists, and once past it the loss is total - including the version history the save confirmation promises is kept. WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED, and why this stays owed rather than banked either way: the manager exposes one editable field, #rm-current-title ('This resume's name', placeholder 'e.g. Maintenance Technician CV'), which is the obvious correct-in-place entry for this view, and it was NOT walked - a rename was neither typed, saved, nor confirmed to persist. Banking this oracle green on the delete-confirm alone would be answering a question about correcting an entry with evidence about preventing a destruction, and banking it red without trying the rename would be calling a gap on a control I did not touch. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS: type a new title into #rm-current-title, save, and confirm it persists and re-renders in the row list (the row title comes from d.title, falling back to 'Untitled resume'); then decide the oracle on that. Consider also whether a delete deserves an undo window given that the same page keeps a version history for every save.

evidence.checked: MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, with the delete held for 700ms so the in-flight window is observable. IN FLIGHT: synchronously after the press the Yes button reads disabled=true, aria-busy='true', label 'Deleting...' - before this session's fix there was NO in-flight state at all, which is precisely what invited the second and third taps that fired duplicate deletes (row 196). TERMINAL: the toast reads 'Resume deleted - it and all of its saved versions are gone for good.' and the list re-renders. FAILURE: with ids that cannot resolve, opening a resume toasts 'Could not open that resume.', leaves the manager OPEN and re-renders the list - so a failed switch does not strand the person on a half-switched page, and switchResume only clears the undo stack and resets the AI panels AFTER loadCloudById succeeds. The delete error path was given the same treatment: the control returns to 'Yes' with aria-busy removed, so a failure is retryable rather than a dead button. NOT CLAIMED: the physical rows leaving the database - every DELETE was intercepted and counted, so what is proven is that the person can tell WHICH outcome happened and when, which is this oracle's subject.

value_checked.in_flight: disabled=true, aria-busy='true', label 'Deleting...' synchronously on press
value_checked.in_flight_before_fix: none - no disable, no label change, no busy state
value_checked.terminal_success: Resume deleted - it and all of its saved versions are gone for good. + list re-render
value_checked.failure_open: Could not open that resume. - manager stays open, list re-renders, undo stack untouched
value_checked.failure_delete: control restored to 'Yes', aria-busy removed - retryable
value_checked.not_claimed: the rows physically leaving the DB - all DELETEs held
